## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This review found only an optional correction: `test_rejects_legacy_header` returns `None` because of the `END` check, not the new version check, so it cannot catch the regression it names. This review read `app/report.py` and `tests/test_report.py` in full and traced each test against the base and head versions of `parse_report`. No tests were run. One strength: `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` uses a complete report with a `REPORT v0` header. The base `startswith("REPORT ")` check accepts that report and the new exact match rejects it, so this test does protect the changed branch.

## Changes
`parse_report` now accepts only the exact header `REPORT v1` instead of any header that starts with `REPORT `. The pull request also adds two tests that check unsupported headers are rejected.

## Suggestions
- tests/test_report.py:10 — tests — Make the legacy-header test reach the version check — The fixture `"REPORT v1\nversion=v1"` passed through `"v0".join(fixture.rsplit("v1", 1))` becomes `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`, which keeps the `v1` header and has no `END` line. `parse_report` therefore returns `None` at `app/report.py:3` (`lines[-1] != "END"`) before it reaches the changed check at `app/report.py:5`. The test passes on both the base and head code. The comment on line 9, "changing the fixture's version to v0", is also wrong: the edit changes the body line, not the header. — Your test suite includes a test named for legacy-header rejection that cannot fail if the version check is removed or loosened, so it adds no regression protection and misleads anyone who reads it. — Fix: Use a complete report with a legacy header, such as `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`, or remove the test, since `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers that case.
